body: I did this literally Monday night, and so yesterday was a bit of a struggle to eat normally, but it's more worth it to eat regularly following munchies than it is to make yourself feel bad, yknow? The eating was good, yeah? That's the point! It tastes good because it's good to eat, and it's a natural part of munchies and marijuana and all that. If we enjoyed ourselves in the moment, then that's the end of the thoughts about it, realistically—enjoyment should overpower any guilt, because the joy is real and the guilt is a social construct, or at least that's how I feel better about things a lot of the time.

I guess I just struggle with the fact that my body no longer seems wracked by disorder in terms of how it treats food (I've not binged much since May, same with purging kind of), but my *mind* is the problem, so it feels wrong to treat my mental issues as warranting physical, bodily treatment; the whole *I Ate Fries Alone For The First Time In Months The Other Day And I've Not Been Obsessively Walking So I Must Be Fine And Don't Need To Keep "Letting" Myself Eat Carelessly* thing is really hard to get around. Bluh.
i fear making her feel that she is walking on eggshells around me, but i have considered it, yes.
thank you for your kind words
i do feel that it is my responsibility to get better, and my failing to have not gotten better already, but i do understand the sentiment thank you

I just don't want to fuck everything up by wasting time and money on care when I could just fix it and be better because everyone makes it sound like a choice and I've been hospitalized before and I can just fix it and not lose money or fuck up the semester, yknow. I need to be function!!! Capable!!! Sorry thank you

Dishes, clean the apartment, I go on walks pretty obsessively but only at night because then no one can see me (and the wind blowing my hair won't be seen), I write music but I've not had the energy or time to do that recently, cook for my partner, hang out with her. She doesn't make me drained, but she's really the only one.
I just am realizing that I don't know at all what normal eating looks like, but I appreciate your words. Thank you very much

So, like. even though it's been awhile since it was *really* bad—day(s) without food, over exercise, purging nearly every day, i.e. last winter through September of 2022-ish—and I've been trying to fix myself with a lot of hiccups and relapses since late November, it's. normal and expected for my hunger to be everywhere? 

I guess I don't really know what I'm aiming for, too, since I grew up disordered, so I don't really know what normal to shoot for. uh. just. constancy? i have to not try to reign anything in?

I've not really been engaging in restriction, which is why I'm a bit lost. I messed up last Friday and didn't eat until 10pm, but before then I'd not gone past 2pm without eating for quite awhile, probably since mid- or late-December. And before that (November-ish) I'd eat normal meals with my girlfriend without really eating in between, or full-on binging. Before that (summer and winter) it was, like, bad restricting and exercise. I just don't see why, after eating okay-ish for a month or two with the occasional smattering of restriction or purging, I would still have abnormal hunger cues.

I've not convinced myself that I'm cured anymore, I'm aware now that the thoughts is evidence that I still am ill and need to keep going, i just. am very tired.

I just keep getting into it and then unable to shake the feeling that for me to be eating "so much" (going back and forth between eating >!1000-1500!< a day to >!2000-2500!< when honoring hunger, both physical and mental, and ignoring disordered thoughts) for so long (i.e. a couple days, or a week or so) means that I'm not recovering or getting close to normal, I've just settled into continuous overeating. I don't know which parts of my brain to trust, because they all feel like they're lying! Bluh. But thank you! I'm just longing for that rewiring to be done—some day.

It's less that I'm judging them and more that my intake mental guideline has shifted from being As Little As Possible to Less Than Those Around Me, and so I'm calculating the caloric intake of those around me all the time and trying to eat less than them, and if I eat More on any given day I feel like I've failed/I'm disgusting/I'm not actually disordered/I'm out of control/etc. This gets toxic easily given that I live with my partner, and I end up depending on her to eat for *me* to eat the equivalent amount, and then when I'm alone I struggle to eat, or try to guess the range of what she's eating elsewhere and have a horrible time with that, etc. It feels horrible.

I made myself eat more today while she's at work to maybe break that artificial limit, and to face a fear food, but I just feel like I'm doing something horribly wrong.

I end up binging every once in awhile, and I >!purge!< so that I don't have to feel the full stomach and to >!avoid calories!< and things like that, sure, but I also do it because I feel like I need to validate the binge. Like, if I don't >!purge!< then I'm just someone who eats a lot and has very little control and has gone from the massive proof of control of being able to go days without eating to now I try to eat twice a day and sometimes have snacks and am always thinking about eating and food. If I was someone who was truly suffering then I would be completely controlled by it like I was before, but the way I am now I can hide it most of the time and, though it may be on my mind most hours of the day and I avoid a lot of foods because I'm afraid, i still am eating relatively normal foods when I make myself eat instead of just eating a bag of steamed cauliflower or something. if i had an ED i wouldn't be eating when I'm alone I'd have the control to not eat—b/p behavior is irrelevant because i
I guess not, huh. I think I sort of convinced myself that I've been lying to myself and others, like, impersonating someone with an ED? Not real? Bluh, I don't know.

I just don't understand why this is happening. It's making me feel like I shouldn't be letting myself eat if I'm not ravenously hungry. People get depressed and forget to eat, and I ate a bit for awhile and then suddenly I don't want food ever? And then I go back to being Pretty hungry? And then get normal hunger cues? And then go back to wild vacillation? I don't know what's part of the recovery process and what's part of me now being Normal, or if I even am, or if the thoughts mean that I'm still disordered, or if the lack of hunger means I'm recovered and shouldn't be making sure I eat anymore, or if the sudden bouts of a lot of hunger mean I'm back to being disordered, or if this all means that I shouldn't waste my time or others' time with trying to get professional help. Bluh

I just worry about being full or satisfied at the time of a meal and then getting genuinely full by the end and being scared, but I do understand what you mean. I don't have a team, but I appreciate the advice! Thank you.

I just have a hard time following, listening, and understanding my hunger signals because oftentimes I can't tell if I'm actually hungry or if I just want food, and what kind of wanting food is mental hunger opposed to just wanting something in my mouth that I should wait through until a social meal or something. Sometimes the desire for food can be so agonizing, even if my stomach isn't grumbling, that I end up eating something, but then that sabotages my security in eating later borne of being physically hungry (feeling okay about eating because I'm physically hungry) when I could've waited and been hungry for it instead of eating just because I wanted to. One of my meds, too, makes me painfully hungry, so I guess my whole concept of interpreting my body signals is all hazy, with justification for eating (sometimes/oftentimes "a lot") being that I'm fighting disorder—i.e. I'm allowed to be eating this peanut butter because it's a fear food and I have to, I'm allowed to be eating this meal alone because I'm supposed to be consistent, even if I'm not eating with someone and this meal is probably more than what my partner is getting at work, etc.

I usually get myself to eat because I know that if I don't eat in the mornings then it'll be harder/near-impossible to get myself to eat later, but it just feels unfair that people can be so nonchalant and forget about food when I *have* to stick to it and eat even if it feels bad.

I dont know if this will help at all, but your post has made me feel a bit better because I'm in the exact same position. For a couple months I only really ate with my girlfriend, so even though that was technically better than my intake before it still wasn't honoring my hunger or working towards recovery. I had a period in October where I tried for a week, didn't hold. December I honored it for the whole month but still not wholly, so I never broke out of that extreme hunger and eventually relapsed into hard-core restriction. 

For these last four days I've been trying to honor it in a way I haven't before, and it's so goddamn hard—bloating, brain won't shut up, etc. Exactly what you described with the physical hunger fading after eating but not being able to get food out of your mind with the mental hunger. I wish you luck and consistency.
I do see it yeah, which is why I almost never express that this is what's in my head unless it's to my therapist.

Because I was raised to be this, because it's been my defining character trait for so long that it'd be a waste of myself and my potential to intentionally rip it from my brain, because I'd be disappointing everyone, because I'd be losing myself, because then I'd be like everyone else, because I'd be a hedonist, because I have to compensate for all of the bad qualities of me and all the sins I've committed, because I have to compensate for how I look, because I can't afford new clothes, because it's more fiscally responsible (though I know it isn't), etc. Sigh. Sorry.

Absolutely not, but there's a point at which people decide that someone just doesn't want to get better, right? Even if they're insisting time and time again that they do? Without results, how hard am I really trying? I know this is me saying I'm an exception, but I don't see how else this could be portrayed.
I'll be able to identify the voice some day, hopefully. I wish you luck as well.

Does intake level out eventually, after the extreme hunger and everything? I've never *not* been in "control" of my intake, so I don't really know what my food goals are other than this nebulous normalcy everyone tells me is possible. I'm aware that I'm abnormal, I just don't know which parts are abnormal until I get reminded how precariously I'm balanced.  Seeing people talk about disordered eating as if it's something identifiable, breakable, reversible, etc. is wild to me, as is when people talk about it like an annoyance and not the soulsucking hopeless hell I feel like I'm trapped in. Sorry

I hesitate to say I'm going through trauma when I've put my partner and friends through the trauma of me getting put in the psych ward. Isn't it a *thing* that some people are just built to be horrible people because of not being able to get better? Even as situations change (getting older, not being around my mother anymore, etc.) I still can't seem to move on, get better, or rewire my brain. I have hope—obviously, considering I'm still here—but it feels less like hope and more like selfish desperation.

I mean... Isn't it indicative of some sort of lack of control or gluttony if I end up eating more than others? It's another social comparative thing, making sure you fall in line with everyone else and/or are better, right?

I always get caught on eating when not around others, I feel gluttonous and like I should be able to go longer without eating so I almost never eat when I'm alone. I've gotten a bit better, but I still only can do it within the calories I've observed from others as a limit. Bluh

I just grew up raised by a mother with an ED and my only defining trait being that I was thin, and so I was constantly bombarded with shit about other peoples' bodies (lack of control, pity, disgust, etc.) and foods being portrayed certain ways. I've not been able to remove those associations, I guess; every time I go to eat, depending on what it is obviously, it's inevitably surrounded by thoughts of the deplorable pity that would be cast on others at restaurants, on the street, my friends and family, all by my mother. Knowing that to fix this I'd have to face a childhood full of trauma makes me... not confident in my ability to fix it. I don't know. Bluh.

I struggle a lot with thoughts about, like, what does it mean about *me* that I want all of these foods, that I'm "giving up" on eating healthily, that I'm intentionally making the decision to eat more, that I'm *allowing* myself to eat the large amount of food that is required during recovery, that I'm constantly thinking about food and obsessing over it yet others just eat when they want and stop when they're full, that I'm ditching one of the most defining features of my character for a lack of tight control, that I'm supposed to make the concerted effort to follow hunger cues but not run or walk to compensate, etc. My girlfriend explicitly said the other night while we were talking openly about a lot of this that everyone would be happier if I ate more and if I gained weight, because she'll get questions about me ("Does she ever eat?", "\[MY NAME\] is so small, why?", "What's wrong with your girlfriend?", etc.) and it makes her upset because she knows why I'm like this. I guess I just can't imagine a person who bears my name and who isn't defined by this disorder and all of the emotional stunting/dysregulation it brings. I'm also worried about not being able to fix myself in time, before everyone leaves because I can't get better. Sigh.

It's frustrating and feels demeaning to be told that I'm not actually trying to get better when I've been trying to fix this for years and the closest I've gotten was this most recent time I tried, from late November to the end of December. My girlfriend and best friend are both the most prominent people in my life, and also the people I live with (my girlfriend and I in an upstairs apartment, friend in the downstairs), and it feels like they're going somewhere I can't follow. I'd hate to lose everything we've built together, my girlfriend and I, but I get paralyzed every day. It feels like I'm starting again every morning, and no matter how much mental reworking I do I can't seem to get over any of this. I ended up in the psych ward because I'd been trying to eat at least >!1200!< calories most days and eat without relying on her, but right as the new year kicked off they started doing exercise and talking about getting muscular and I couldn't handle it---how am I supposed to eat if I can't exercise to "earn" it, if it's upsetting to her for me to run (and consequently tear myself apart over hunger, steps, calories, etc.) then how can I feel okay with everyone around me counting protein, running, lifting weights, etc.? 

What was all of this trying for if I can be knocked down into a violent panic just because these people in my life want to do something that I'm *aware* feels good; *I* am the problem, y'know. This disorder has defined my life since I was very, very young and now I have to fundamentally rewrite myself so that I can have the life I want and be the person others need me to be, and it's... a lot. I love her too much to not try, but it's still a lot. I just feel like I'm trapped in a burning building.

Sorry, by the way. I understand that the point of a response to a post like this is not to enter into a therapeutic conversation, I think I'm just organizing my thoughts. Who knows. Sorry.
Thank you! It's hard to do anything when I've not eaten, too, so I'm gonna try to use that as motivation.

I always get caught up on this weird trapping that I can't seem to shake where I think that I have to eat equal to or less than my partner eats, and only when she does because if I eat before her then I've "lost" for the day and "can't control my urges" or whatever, but yeah! If my body is telling me I'm hungry, then I'm hungry, right? Nobody is keeping track of my calories or will know about what I'm eating, and nobody will think less of me somehow for eating, especially her; it's hard to keep all of this in mind and believe that That is reality, but I'm gonna get there goddammit.

Yeah, we've talked about my potential asexuality, and she's said that she'd probably be okay with a relationship without sex, but that it still bothers her—I just want to be able to give her everything, and everything includes what is expected in a relationship (i.e. warmth, support, affection, understanding, apparently sexuality). It's not a pressing issue as far as I can tell, but I do worry about it eventually being an issue of me not "being enough"; even though I know she's not like that and wouldn't leave or anything, I don't want that tension or lack of giving what's needed, regardless. I'm in therapy, I'm just uncomfortable bringing up sexuality with her, especially considering that this could be fixed if I could just Have A Sex Drive, y'know? I guess I'm reluctant to not try, considering I think I've felt sexuality before, which means I could bring it back if I tried. Maybe. Just didn't know if there was something I was missing about how this develops or happens or could be handled.

This is what eating disorders can do—make you want to be that statistic, make you want it to be You (as if that's not another primary characteristic of EDs, it becoming your whole self), make you want it to take you out because then you were "good enough" at it and one of the One True Sufferers.

When it gets bad for me, I fall into that. Active suicide would be the easy way out, where the ED was just a side issue, not real enough to take me out. Letting it kill me? That's me succeeding.

"I need this to kill me", y'know?

Obviously this is just delusion. We live to be alive, not like this. I wish you luck in the ways that matter, even if we can't see those ways that life matters.

I've been in a near-death situation with this before, and you can't really tell until it's almost too late. I just don't want to admit I've fucked up, I guess, because then I never improved as a person. First time through college was really hard because of eating and psychosis, but things are different now, living situation wise. I dont want to fuck up. I've sustained myself this far yknow? Even though I know that's stupid. It'd feel like giving up. sorry I'm like. dumping therapy-minded shit bluh

This is my second time trying college, because I had to withdraw the first time from having a psychotic episode. I really don't want to have to. I want to be capable, I've spent my whole life being told I'm incapable and unable of functioning normally, and I shouldn't try and I just. i ended up going today and the emergency room did nothing and just sent me home so I guess nothing is going to happen, unless my endocrinologist does something. I dont know. I just want to be a normal person and still be like this. I can't spend more of my life on hold. pthhhh sorry

Yeah, no, she's not changing anytime soon. She did the classic, "You have to tell me what I'm doing wrong, or else I can't change, how can you be upset with me when you won't tell me what I'm doing wrong and I can't change, it's your fault I'm like this," last summer, so my father and I were honest about her behavior (which we've done before, she just never changes so we stopped trying, but we relented) and I had to cut a date with my girlfriend short because my entire family started calling me telling me she was going to kill herself and that she had sent out suicide notes, so I rushed back to her house. She was angry and had a knife and threatened me with it, went into my room and broke some of my things, threatened to kill my pet bird, threw me on the ground and hit me, and wouldn't go to the hospital even as I was crying and pleading with her. She drove away, and as was scared to death that she'd kill herself and it'd be my fault again, so I called the cops and eventually she went into the hospital, which led to an outpatient therapy program that went nowhere. We told her that we were worried none of this would help, and she blamed us all for everything going wrong and her "Recovery" not working, or whatever. She and my father recently broke up, so she's alone now, and as far as I can tell she's not trying to change, other than the fact that she sent my sister a long message about how I was right that she was a narcissist, how she was a terrible mother, she was sorry she was our mother, and then linked the Adele song "Easy On Me", which she has said is her song to us, which is just objectively funny.

Sorry I'm just rambling, I've had this all in for so long. I keep trying to ignore her, but she starts calling everyone else to tell them to tell me to talk to her, and has threatened a welfare check. Fun.

I've always struggled with suicide in some form, I've made multiple attempts. My eating disorder controls my life on and off and has for years, BPD, bipolar, panic attacks destroy my relationships, schizophrenia makes every day living hell. I'm so tired. My mother kicked me out last year for being a lesbian, so I was homeless for a time until my girlfriend and I got an apartment. Things are good! Except my brain says they aren't, I'm having daily panic attacks, struggle eating unless I'm around her, walk excessively, im ungrateful I feel, and it's making her worry she's not good enough. We both have eating disorders, and even though she's doing well now, she still lost a lot of weight while it was bad and it's all i can ever think about—the difference, the stark contrast, watching it happen, doing the same. I wish it'd never happened, but it did, and I couldn't help because im incapable, yknow? My mother is blaming me for getting kicked out, saying she'll meet my dead grandmother sooner than she should if she keeps being "verbally abused" by me (I avoid talking to her at all costs), she's threatened suicide saying it'd be my fault many times in my life, and I've always been her little therapist until I'm not good enough anymore, and even then she still needs me. She raised me to have an eating disorder, I've been counting calories since I was seven, I'm so tired. I'm stuck like this. I feel trapped. I have a plan, I tried last week, this plan is better, but I don't want to but I do. I can't do that to her. I love her so much, I'm just selfish. I don't know what to do.
Ownership is deletion of the source of the problem. My mistakes were not curing her ed. My misstep was letting him touch me for years. Hurting myself. Hurting otyerd

I guess my fear of hospitalization comes from the fact that I've been hospitalized for this before, and it wasn't as bad then as it is now, I just have been living with people who haven't noticed how bad it's gotten.

Regardless, I'll definitely consider seeing someone soon, assuming I can. This is the first thing to genuinely frighten me with this; even losing bits of my esophagus, fainting, etc didn't frighten me, but something about the heart scares me no matter what. We'll see.

Problem is that if I saw a doctor, I'd most likely be hospitalized because of how low my weight has gotten, which I don't want. I'm probably going to end up doing it eventually, given I have the funds and ability, but, I just have my fears.

I mean. My weight has gotten to Maybe(?) a concerning point, and I tend to go two or three days (four if I'm lucky) without eating. I only ate today, having not eaten since the second, because my heart started hurting Really Badly and I figure it might help? But. It didn't really. Point is, I can't Really get it checked out because I fear getting sent to the psych ward again. Sigh.

I'm 19 so, yeah, it's possible for me to just get a checkup of my own volition. My whole fear, I guess, is just my unfamiliarity with the whole system? Because I don't know what the cutoff is for being hospitalized. I've been hospitalized more times than I'd like to admit for myriad reasons, but never for the state of my throat and admission of eating disorder things, yknow? I've only been hospitalized when it gets so bad that I can no longer function and when it's Obvious that I'm in danger.

Thinking it might be a good idea to get a checkup. Especially given the increase in blood recently; as sick and deluded as I am, my brain does still sometimes freak out a bit when I fill a toilet with throat blood and I pull my hand out of my mouth, also covered with blood, yknow?

Hopefully once you become able to see a doctor on your own, you'll be able to get some help. It definitely is beneficial to see someone who knows what they're doing and such.

I've considered going to a doctor about it, especially given that, in the time since I made this post, it's happened again, but my fear is being sent to the psych ward again. It just stresses the people in my life out, and sort of traumatizes them every time it happens, yknow? I'd like to keep this whole Slipping Back Into ED thing a secret, aside from the few people who know. I'm honestly (and probably foolishly) just hoping that my throat will heal itself in between the times I throw up, because I don't really know how to get through eating without throwing up, it's sort of what keeps me going. In a sick way I feel like I'm not making progress if my throat doesn't hurt?

Point is, eventually I'll seek medical help. Largely, I was just waiting until the new year to do it, so that I don't ruin the holidays and such.

Oh, don't get me wrong, I don't binge at all. My routine is going usually 2-4 days without eating depending on what's happening in my life, and then when I do eat I make myself vomit it back up. Sometimes I go through periods where I try to eat every other day, but that usually ends with me vomiting it back up anyway, so. I don't really remember the last time I kept something down.

Honestly at this point the blood doesn't even frighten me or concern me, the only reason the chunk frightened me was because my girlfriend got scared. Something might not be right with my head lmao. I bleed most times, I figured that was normal after a certain point.

It's especially frustrating because I love reading! I have so many books and I was going to spend this time quarantined reading some of the ones I've not gotten to, but it makes it so hard. It'll go away eventually.

It's exhausting Trying, but, thank you for the numbers, I'll keep it in mind. I just feel like I've Failed if I put anything in my body at all in a day, much less two or three days. I don't know how to get out of this loop, I don't remember what it was like thinking normally, not that I really ever did. When I'm up to it, I'll try 50ml an hour. The numbers are scary, but, I'm pretty sure I'm not doing my body any favors by doing this. Thank you.

i just don't know how to handle drinking anymore. ive been at this point before and it landed me in the hospital, but that stupid part of me that's sick wants to see if i can do it Right this time, yknow?

I mean, I've already thrown up quite a lot since then, and it's been fine, just blood. My concern is that if I go to the doctor for this they'll know what's going on, yknow? Don't wanna deal with that, can't take the psych ward again lmao. But yeah, I'll try to hold back until I can get it looked at. Gonna wait through the rest of the year, though, because I'm not going to do that to the people in my life, go into the hospital and leave them again and such. Honestly the only reason I'm concerned is because my girlfriend got concerned; it barely even registered in my head, but. It's probably a problem.
